newsitem.title: CANADA: Minister orders CAW vote on CAI.
newsitem.headline: Minister orders CAW vote on CAI.

text.p: Canadian Labor Minister Alfonso Gagliano said on Wednesday he used his power to order members of the Canadian Auto Workers union to vote on a tough restructuring plan to save troubled Canadian Airlines Corp.

"We are at an impasse and 16,000 jobs are at stake here. So that's why I directed the Canada Labor Relations Board to organize a vote for the employees of Canadian Airlines who are members of the Canadian Automobile Workers union..." Gagliano told parliament during questioning from opposition parties.

The CAW, representing about 3,700 of Canadian's 16,400 employees, is the only union that has refused to endorse Canadian's restructuring plan, calling instead for a government bailout for the airline.
A meeting among Transport Minister David Anderson, Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson and CAW president Buzz Hargrove on Wednesday morning failed to produce any change in Hargrove's position.
"I directed the board according to the authority that is given me under Article 107 of the Canadian Labor Code," Gagliano said in response to a question by Reform Party transport spokesman Jim Gouk.
A CAW spokeswomand said the union had no immediate response to Gagliano's announcement.
Hargrove told reporters earlier he would not allow members of his union to vote on the restructuring scheme.
Transport Minister David Anderson ruled out any government bailout for the cash-strapped company other than the fuel tax rebate he offered last week.
"It is important for us to remember...that Canadian Airlines is not yet in a position where it is assured of success," Anderson said in parliament.

"We trust that a vote of the Canadian Auto Workers who are employed by Canadian Airlines will result in a positive result. We are of course not sure. We do not know how they will vote," Anderson added. "...If Canadian is to survive, we need cooperation on all parties to move forward with the restructuring proposal to turn this company from a company which had chronic losses that totaled over C$1.3 billion to one in the black which makes money."
